01Slot breakout routed

The whole X68000 expansion bus on two ribbon cables: 2 × 50 gold fingers, six SN74LVC8T245 level translators, two 2 × 20 IDC headers. Plug an FPGA or MCU board on the other end and it becomes any expansion card you like. Built first because it proves the three mechanical unknowns — the finger footprint, the 45° bevel and the card-guide fit — for a few dollars.

Not ready to order 6 GND connections still need a via each, placed by hand in pcbnew with the ratsnest showing. Beyond that: there is no schematic, so ERC has never run; the finger geometry is copied from midiori and has never been in a real slot; hard gold and the bevel are order notes that are not in the gerbers; and the BOM's LCSC column is deliberately empty. The full list is in docs/FAB-BREAKOUT.md.

02Where the other half is

There is no companion board yet, and that is on purpose rather than an oversight. The breakout's ribbons are meant to reach a dev board you already own — the Tang Console 138K for the logic, a Tang Nano 9K for the PSRAM timing. The memory and MIDI as a product is the card below, which carries the FPGA, its in-package 8 MB PSRAM and the MIDI drivers all by itself and does not use the breakout at all.

The two-board option the right-angle headers open up With the ribbons leaving in the plane of the card rather than up into the neighbouring slot, a second PCB can sit behind this one in the same slot, joined by a short ribbon: this card carries the fingers, the translators and the plane split; the logic card carries the FPGA, the memory and the MIDI jacks. Revising the logic half then costs one small board instead of a 150 mm one, and the breakout is the same PCB whether the other end is a Tang Console on the bench or the finished card in the machine. Not committed to — the single-card design is still the plan — but the headers no longer rule it out.

03X68000 MIDI card netlist only

What it is

Two MIDI ports on 3.5 mm TRS-A jacks at $EAFA00 and $EAFA10, plus 8 MB of main-memory expansion, on one card — a Gowin GW1NR-9 with its PSRAM in the package doing all of it.

The gateware is finished and tested: real 68000 bus cycles in, decoded MIDI bytes out, 48 pysim tests including a driver probe sequence and an interrupt-acknowledge vector read.

Where it stands

Netlist66 parts, 134 nets
FPGA pins60 of 63 used
Gateware48 tests passing
Layoutnot started

Bank 3 of the QN88P must run at 1.8 V because it carries the PSRAM, and JTAG lives there — which splits the address bus 15 lines at 1.8 V and 8 at 3.3 V, and means the programmer has to drive 1.8 V.

04Slot cover plate drawn

176 × 20 × 2 mm, outline taken from midiori's — a known-good fit — with the hole sizes and positions measured out of their STL rather than guessed. Three 3.5 mm bores at 22 mm pitch; the middle one sits exactly where theirs does, so that one's clearance is proven.
